summary: The recorded base reproduced the exact seeded min-p assertion on gfx950. At the exact candidate commit, its regression and an independent combined-filter numerical reference passed. The candidate fully fixes the original internal PyTorch sampling contract by removing an invalid assertion; filtered tokens remain impossible and sorted samples map to original vocabulary IDs.

tests.what_was_measured: Exact failing-before reproduction on the recorded base, from the repository sampler source, with the reported AssertionError before sampling.
Candidate regression: three GPU cases for repeatability, retained support and vocabulary mapping, normalization invariance, and the inclusive threshold/top-k boundary.

Independent 4,096-row combined top-k/top-p/min-p case matched an explicitly normalized deterministic reference exactly, replayed exactly, excluded the filtered ID, and the original fixture returned only IDs 1 and 3.

gpu_evidence: AMD Instinct MI350X, gfx950/capability (9, 5), ROCm 7.2, torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2; candidate regression and independent numerical assertions executed on GPU.
native_rebuild_reason: No native C++, HIP, or FlyDSL source changed; repository-environment.json also specifies no separate native artifact.
remaining_limitations: Validated on one assigned gfx950 GPU only; no cross-architecture, multi-GPU, or multi-node claim is made.
No model-weight or HTTP serving run was performed; the evidence directly exercises the original issue's internal PyTorch sampling function and does not establish model semantic accuracy.
Torch emitted a non-fatal Dynamo metrics serialization traceback during the independent run; all numerical assertions still completed and the process exited zero.
Mirror main was a207786205bff0919eb2c8c9126c67f302ccff34 at review time, while failing-before evidence intentionally uses the mandated recorded base.
